introH2: 🌿 What kind of stays does Khao Sok in Surat Thani have, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: Khao Sok is a tropical rainforest known as one of the oldest rainforests in Thailand, with steep limestone karsts, the cool clear Sok River, and Cheow Lan Lake, where limestone peaks rise out of emerald-green water so strikingly it's earned the nickname the Guilin of Thailand · what confuses many people is that Khao Sok stays split into two clear kinds · the first, floating rafthouses in the middle of Cheow Lan Lake — the prettiest views, but you have to drive to Ratchaprapha Dam pier and then take a longtail boat in, power/air-con/wifi are limited for stretches, and many require you to come on a package · the second, jungle lodges along the Sok River in Khlong Sok village — you drive right up to the door, walk into the national park gate, go river tubing or rafting, or use it as a base for a day trip out to the lake · Getting there: take a minivan/taxi from Surat Thani town, about 1.5 hrs, or from Phuket/Krabi/Khao Lak about 2.5–3 hrs, to Khlong Sok · we've ranked this list by real guest review scores, rounding up 8 stays we've reviewed in depth, giving both the good points and the honest caveats, comparing prices across 3 sites with direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Khao Sok is reached mainly by road — take a minivan/taxi from Surat Thani town (~1.5 hrs) or Phuket/Krabi/Khao Lak (~2.5–3 hrs) to Khlong Sok village (the national park gate) · jungle lodges along the Sok River = you drive right up to the door, and can walk into the national park / go rafting / go tubing · Cheow Lan Lake rafthouses = you drive on another ~1 hr to Ratchaprapha Dam pier and then take a longtail boat ~1–1.5 hrs to the raft (many require you to come on a tour/package) · out on the raft, power/air-con/wifi are limited for stretches, but the views and quiet are more than worth it · ⚠️ the recommended window is the dry season, Dec–Apr, but the rainforest is green and lovely all year, so be ready for rain/mosquitoes/humidity.

faqTitle: FAQ — questions travellers often ask about staying in Khao Sok, Surat Thani

faq.q: ❓ How do you get to Khao Sok, and which route is easiest?
faq.a: Khao Sok is reached mainly by road, with no airport of its own · take a minivan/taxi from Surat Thani town, about 1.5 hrs, or from Phuket, Krabi and Khao Lak, about 2.5–3 hrs, to Khlong Sok village, which is the national park gate and where almost all the jungle lodges are · to go and sleep on a Cheow Lan Lake raft, you drive on another hour or so to Ratchaprapha Dam pier, then take a longtail boat in · people usually fly into Phuket/Surat Thani and connect by road, or stop at Khao Sok on the way between Phuket and Koh Samui

faq.q: ❓ Should you pick a Cheow Lan Lake raft, or a jungle lodge in Khlong Sok?
faq.a: It depends on what you want · floating rafthouses in the middle of Cheow Lan Lake (like Panvaree, 500 Rai, Praiwan, Khao Sok Rafthouse) give you the prettiest Guilin-style karst-over-water views, a once-in-a-lifetime experience, but you need a boat transfer, power/signal are limited, and you usually have to come on a package · jungle lodges along the Sok River at Khlong Sok (like Our Jungle House, Anurak, Las Orquideas, Montania) you drive right up to the door, and can walk into the national park, go rafting or tubing, and they have more complete power/air-con/Wi-Fi · with 2 nights, many people sleep at a lodge for 1 night + a raft for 1 night

faq.q: ❓ To sleep on a raft in the middle of Cheow Lan Lake, do you have to book a tour?
faq.a: Mostly yes · because the rafts float in the middle of the lake inside the national park, reached only by longtail boat, many rafts sell as a 2D1N package that includes the car + boat transfers from Ratchaprapha Dam pier, all meals, and activities like an early-morning nature boat trip, a cave tour and kayaking · a few, like Praiwan Raft House, let you book a room room-only for a single night and arrange your own boat/tour, but you still have to get to the pier yourself · always check before booking whether the rate includes the boat transfers and meals

faq.q: ❓ When is the best time for Khao Sok, can you visit in the rainy season?
faq.a: The recommended window with the calmest weather is the dry season, December–April, with less rain, convenient hiking and boat trips, but prices are high and rooms/rafts fill fast, so book ahead · that said, Khao Sok is a rainforest, so it can rain all year and turns lush green in the rainy season, and many nature lovers like the misty atmosphere and the waterfalls at this time · whenever you go, be ready for rain, mosquitoes and humidity, and pack a rain jacket, mosquito repellent and shoes you can get wet

faq.q: ❓ Should you stay 1 night or 2 nights in Khao Sok?
faq.a: If you're really short on time, 1 night is enough to see the highlights, but if you can choose, 2 nights is much better value, because Khao Sok has both worlds to experience · the popular plan is a first night at a jungle lodge in Khlong Sok (like Our Jungle House or Montania), hiking, rafting and tubing on the Sok River · a second night on a boat to a Cheow Lan Lake raft (like Panvaree or Khao Sok Rafthouse), an early-morning boat trip past the limestone karsts and a cave tour · getting to the lake takes half a day, so a single night on the raft can feel rushed
